notes: The San Francisco Portrait Photograph Collection, read whole to settle the question #217 left open: the dossier had written SFP 136 off unread on the assumption that a portrait collection raises the SFP 130 problem, where the caption's subject is a named living person and redacting the name leaves nothing but a household at a street number. Measured, it is a different problem and a much smaller one. 2,615 of 2,664 records are a person and no place at all, and the addressed remainder is not households: it is three public figures at three public buildings, half a century dead, each already documented in published sources. The other seven candidates are a caption's own numbers reading as street numbers — a fundraising drive named for its year ("1949 Career Drive", "1944 War Fund Drive"), a vacuum cleaner model, an exposition, a highway association.

coverage.remaining: None. Every record in SFP 136 was read. With this batch every collection in DigitalSF that holds an addressed record has been read or, in SFP 130's case, closed unread with the reason recorded.
coverage.note: Read 2,664 catalogue records — the whole collection. 2,615 carry a personal name subject and no street number and were skipped at extraction. 10 candidate addresses came out, of which 3 are real street addresses and 7 are a caption's own figures; 2 resolved to a parcel and both were published. The third, a photograph in front of 1000 Van Ness Avenue, is dated "19--" and carries no year at all.
